en: Dependent on a wholesome state that is co-existent with consciousness, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor co-existent with consciousness by way of root condition... five.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is co-existent with consciousness, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor co-existent with consciousness by way of root condition... five.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is co-existent with consciousness, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor co-existent with consciousness by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to the root condition (hetu), there are thirteen; with respect to the object condition (ārammaṇa), nine ... pe ... with respect to the ripening condition (vipāka), three ... pe ... with respect to the non-disappearance condition (avigata), thirteen.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is not co-existent with consciousness (nocittasahabhu), a state that is neither wholesome nor co-existent with consciousness arises by way of the root condition ... five.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not co-existent with consciousness, a state that is neither unwholesome nor co-existent with consciousness arises by way of the root condition ... five.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is not co-nascent with consciousness, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor co-nascent with consciousness by way of root condition... three. (Abbreviated.
Thirteen in the case of roots, nine in the case of objects... pe ... three in the case of resultants... pe ... thirteen in the case of non-disappearance.
